title: Missing ticket stub
prompt:
A raffle sold tickets numbered 0 to n, and stubs holds the n stubs collected afterwards in any order. Every number appears at most once, and exactly one stub is missing. Return the missing number.

- stubs has 1 to 100,000 distinct integers, each between 0 and n, where n is the length of stubs.
- Target O(n) time and O(1) extra space. You may rearrange stubs in place.
hints: With values 0 to n and n slots, value v can live at index v. Only the value n has no slot.
Swap each value v < n to index v until every such value is home. Leave n where it lands.
Scan for the first index k with stubs[k] != k. If every index matches, the missing number is n.

solution.explanation: Each value v below n has a home at index v, so cyclic sort places it there with one swap. The value n has no slot and stays wherever it lands, which is exactly the slot of the missing number. A final scan finds the first index that does not hold its own value; if all match, n is the one missing.

complexity.notes: Every swap puts one value home for good, so there are at most n swaps. The sum formula n(n + 1) / 2 minus the total, or XOR of indexes and values, also works in O(1) space without rearranging.

followUps: Solve it without changing stubs, using arithmetic or XOR.
Two stubs are missing instead of one. Return both.
